added: This section specifies replay, re-running the ordinary loop on a recorded input trace, so that a recorded session can be inspected, its errors reproduced and its run continued live.
A trace is the primary record of a session, a fixed trace header plus the batches drained at each frame.
A batch is a device's staged set of writes, and a device is any attached participant in the periphery.
A frame is one iteration of the loop, from drain to publication.
The drain is the frame-top swap that applies staged device writes to the root inputs.
The root inputs are the root component's own inputs, the only thing the periphery may write.
The parts below cover the one substitution replay makes, halting and the input mode (where the drain takes its batches from) across halts, what stays the loop's, and the validation up front.
They then cover the what-if replay, re-driving the recorded inputs through a modified model, with the `restore = false` form, which attaches the feed to the simulation as it stands.
The rejected shapes close the section.

(the initialization boundary at `t₀`)
A condition is the datum that says "set this build to this state".

A face is the name a port wears on its component's boundary.

Under `restore = false` the new trace's header is the simulation's own checkpoint (below).
